[K-UPWELL#3] Southwest monsoon upwelling off the west coast of India: Small plankton-feeding pelagic fish, above all the Indian oil sardine, depend on this seasonal production. Fishery scientists commonly relate oil sardine recruitment and landings to upwelling intensity and chlorophyll in the same or the previous season.

[K-SARDINE#2] Indian oil sardine (Sardinella longiceps) fishery: Oil sardine landings swing widely from year to year. ICAR-CMFRI landing estimates show high catches in the early 2010s followed by steep declines in the mid-2010s and again around 2019 to 2021. Proposed drivers include weak upwelling, warm sea surface temperature during El Nino years, and fishing pressure on juveniles.

[K-SARDINE#3] Indian oil sardine (Sardinella longiceps) fishery: Because the species lives only a few years, a poor spawning or recruitment season shows up in the catch quickly, often with a lag of about one year.
